relation_statement: A parameter may be consumed in forward only after its own coordinator's allgather completes; train and eval coordinators must not observe each other's in-flight handles.
observable_signal: stale parameter checksums (values unchanged from the previous mode's shards) in the first iteration after a train/eval switch
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 3 with prefetch/overlap_comm and alternating model.train()/model.eval() inside a step
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO3 InflightParamRegistry shared between train and eval coordinators causes stale handles on mode switch
evidence_from_fix: both coordinators were constructed with the same shared InflightParamRegistry; on mode switch one coordinator observed the other's in-flight handles, leading to silently-stale parameter values

relation_statement: The loss broadcast receive buffer on non-last PP stages must have the same dtype as the sent loss tensor so every stage observes the same loss value.
observable_signal: loss value on non-last PP stages compared against the last stage's aggregated loss (equality check per step)
validity_precondition: pipeline parallel with a bf16 model loss tensor and loss aggregation broadcast to all stages
evidence_from_issue: Pipeline parallel _aggregate_total_loss broadcasts torch.stack of mixed-dtype losses, non-last stages receive wrong dtype
evidence_from_fix: the broadcast tensor was bf16 but other ranks initialised their receive buffer as fp32; dist.broadcast wrote bf16 bytes into an fp32 tensor and other PP stages saw garbage scalar losses

relation_statement: GatedDeltaNet A_log/dt_bias must receive the GDN-prescribed init rather than uninitialized empty memory or default linear init under guard: hybrid model with GatedDeltaNet mixer.
observable_signal: A_log/dt_bias values after init (finite, on-distribution) vs uninitialized/NaN memory.
validity_precondition: hybrid model includes GatedDeltaNet, block init used generic InitMethod path
evidence_from_issue: GatedDeltaNet A_log/dt_bias initialized as empty (uninit memory) and miss the GDN-prescribed init
evidence_from_fix: generic InitMethod did not delegate to the mixer, so params fell back to torch.empty or default inits

relation_statement: Router combine weights must be post-softmax probabilities bounded in [0,1], not raw logits, whenever top-k gating selects and weights experts.
observable_signal: gate/combine weight values falling outside [0,1] (negative or greater than one, as raw logits can be)
validity_precondition: MoE top-k gating module active in forward
evidence_from_issue: TopKGate applies topk to logits instead of post-softmax gates
evidence_from_fix: torch.topk(logits, k) selects experts from raw logits, not softmax probabilities

relation_statement: All parameters must carry the designed init (reset_parameters applied) rather than FSDP default/zero fill under guard: meta-device init with FSDP.
observable_signal: Per-parameter statistics (std, all-zero/uninitialized check) after FSDP materialization.
validity_precondition: torch>=2.1, FSDP wrapping with init_device='meta'
evidence_from_issue: Missing reset_parameters() after FSDP wrap on torch>=2.1 leaves model with default-initialized weights
evidence_from_fix: FSDP no longer auto-calls reset_parameters; params left uninitialized/zero-filled, destroying init scheme

relation_statement: The cached index file must be read as a complete, consistent artifact (atomic write, deterministic ordering) despite concurrent writers under guard: shared work_dir.
observable_signal: Index file completeness/consistency and ordering identity across concurrent runs.
validity_precondition: multiple jobs share work_dir, SamplingInstanceSource rank-0 builds indices
evidence_from_issue: SamplingInstanceSource cache write race — concurrent ladder runs overwrite each other's index files
evidence_from_fix: rank-0 always rewrote via tmp_path.replace, racing so training read partially-written/shuffled indices

relation_statement: Gradient reduction must communicate in the configured communication_data_type (matching bf16 grads) rather than a hard-coded fp16 downcast.
observable_signal: dtype of tensors handed to the allreduce vs configured communication dtype; Inf/0 saturation of out-of-fp16-range gradient values
validity_precondition: bf16 model under ZeRO 1/2/3 with communication dtype expected to be bf16
evidence_from_issue: allreduce_bucket hard-codes communication_data_type=fp16 — bf16 grads silently downcast for reduction
evidence_from_fix: caller never passed self.communication_data_type, so all reductions converted bf16 grads to fp16; values outside fp16's range become Inf/0 and the rest lose precision

relation_statement: Leftover indices must partition disjointly and completely across DataLoader workers under guard: drop_last=False and num_workers>1.
observable_signal: Union and pairwise overlap of per-worker leftover index sets vs full leftover set.
validity_precondition: IterableDataset with drop_last=False, device_batch_size set, num_workers>1, indices not divisible by batch size
evidence_from_issue: IterableDataset leftover indices distributed wrongly across workers
evidence_from_fix: contiguous slice made workers overlap and miss leftovers; fix uses strided slicing so each worker picks its share

relation_statement: The shared cached loss mask must remain unchanged across samples; per-sample in-place padding modifications must operate on a private copy.
observable_signal: checksum of the cached loss mask across successive dataset __getitem__ calls (mutates after the first padded sample)
validity_precondition: cached-mask branch (create_attention_mask=False) with padded sequences over multiple steps of the same dataset
evidence_from_issue: GPTDataset returns aliased cached_loss_mask; downstream in-place padding mutates the shared cache and corrupts later samples
evidence_from_fix: loss_mask was returned by reference instead of a clone; the first sample with padding silently mutates the shared cache, so every subsequent sample starts from a polluted mask

relation_statement: Every rank in a model-parallel group must receive the training batch broadcast from the true first global rank of its DP group under non-contiguous parallel layouts.
observable_signal: input batch checksum equality across ranks that share the same broadcast group
validity_precondition: non-trivial parallel layout where DP groups are not contiguous global ranks (e.g. PP=2, DP=2)
evidence_from_issue: get_data_parallel_src_rank uses global_rank % num_dp_groups instead of looking up first global rank in the DP group
evidence_from_fix: formula only matches the true DP src rank when DP groups are contiguous; with PP > 1 or other interleavings, the formula returns the wrong rank

relation_statement: Each gradient element must be scaled by exactly 1/dp_size once (per its own bucket), not once per bucket over the whole buffer, during gradient reduce preprocessing.
observable_signal: gradient magnitude after preprocessing vs expected 1/dp_size scaling (cumulative (1/dp_size)^num_buckets on affected ranges)
validity_precondition: Megatron-FSDP with multiple buckets per gradient buffer and gradient scaling factor != 1.0
evidence_from_issue: GradReducePipeline scales gbuf.data instead of bucket.data, applying gradient scaling to the wrong tensor span
evidence_from_fix: preprocessing divided every byte of the joint gradient buffer once per bucket, yielding cumulative scaling of (1/dp_size)**num_buckets instead of (1/dp_size), with no shape mismatch

relation_statement: q_norm and k_norm must be constructed with the same elementwise_affine flag equal to the configured value under guard: QK norm enabled.
observable_signal: Presence/absence of learnable scale/bias parameters in q_norm vs k_norm vs config.attention_layer_norm_with_affine.
validity_precondition: attention_layer_norm=True and attention_layer_norm_with_affine=False
evidence_from_issue: q_norm forced to elementwise_affine=True regardless of attention_layer_norm_with_affine
evidence_from_fix: k_norm used config flag but q_norm hard-coded True, breaking q/k symmetry and adding unrequested params

relation_statement: Parameters loaded from a checkpoint must equal the saved values (loading must be idempotent, applying no additional muP rescaling) when resuming a muP model.
observable_signal: Post-load parameter checksums/norms vs checkpoint contents; weights uniformly shrunk/grown by the muP width factor after from_checkpoint witnesses the double rescale.
validity_precondition: model.use_mup=true and OLMo.from_checkpoint() used to resume
evidence_from_issue: muP set_base_shapes rescales parameters again when loading from a checkpoint, doubling the muP scaling
evidence_from_fix: parameters are already in muP-scaled space, so the rescale fires a second time and silently shrinks/grows weights by the muP factor; fix adds mup_rescale_params=False from from_checkpoint

relation_statement: Every trainable submodule's weight-gradient computation must be invoked exactly once per backward pass under fine-grained backward_dw scheduling with latent MoE projections enabled.
observable_signal: Per-parameter main_grad norm of the latent projection weights: exactly zero across all microbatches/steps (and parameter values frozen at init) witnesses the missing gradient computation.
validity_precondition: MoE layer with moe_latent_size set and separate backward_dw scheduling for routed/shared experts
evidence_from_issue: Latent MoE backward_dw never calls fc1_latent_proj/fc2_latent_proj.backward_dw, so gradient for the latent projection weights is silently zero
evidence_from_fix: MoELayer.backward_dw only invoked self.experts.backward_dw() ... latent projection layers were never asked to compute their weight gradients, so their main_grad stayed at zero; the optimizer applied (lr * 0) every step

relation_statement: Layers explicitly pinned to bf16 must execute their GEMMs in bf16 (never be cast into FP8/FP4 paths) even when global low-precision training and CUDA-graph capture are enabled.
observable_signal: Compute dtype / quantization wrapping of the captured attention-linear GEMMs: FP8 cast applied to a keep-in-bf16 module witnesses the violation.
validity_precondition: Mamba/hybrid model with keep-mamba-stack-attention-linear-in-bf16 and config.fp8 or config.fp4 enabled with CUDA graph capture
evidence_from_issue: enables FP8 capture for keep-mamba-stack-attention-linear-in-bf16 layers, casting frozen-bf16 attention linears into FP8 inside the captured graph
evidence_from_fix: set self.fp8_enabled unconditionally ... capturing those layers with FP8 enabled wrapped their GEMMs in FP8 cast paths, silently quantizing weights that were intentionally meant to stay in bf16

relation_statement: The number of tokens entering each expert must match the router's tokens_per_expert counts when no quantization requires alignment padding.
observable_signal: permuted token buffer length vs sum(tokens_per_expert) (extra zero padding tokens entering experts)
validity_precondition: MoE fused permute path with tokens_per_expert provided on non-quantized models (no FP8/FP4)
evidence_from_issue: MoE permute pads tokens unnecessarily for non-quantized dispatch
evidence_from_fix: get_align_size_for_quantization defaulted to 16 even for non-quantized models, padding tokens to multiples of 16, leading to extra zero tokens entering experts and slightly different expert outputs

relation_statement: The FFN output must equal the reference gated computation silu(w1(h)) * w3(h) under guard that a SwiGLU-style gated FFN is configured.
observable_signal: elementwise difference between the module output and a reference SwiGLU computation on the same inputs
validity_precondition: boundary-predictor FFN configured as SwiGLU; applies whenever the gated FFN path executes
evidence_from_issue: F.silu called with two arguments — silu treats w3(h) as inplace flag, drops gating
evidence_from_fix: the intended SwiGLU gate (silu(w1(h)) * w3(h)) never executed, so the FFN computed silu(w1(h)) alone

relation_statement: Checkpoint retention must evict oldest first and never delete the just-saved newest checkpoint under guard: keep-count reached.
observable_signal: Whether the most recently saved checkpoint directory still exists after the retention/deletion loop.
validity_precondition: save_num_checkpoints_to_keep>0 and list already at capacity when a new save fires
evidence_from_issue: Newest checkpoint deleted by retention policy because it is appended after pruning
evidence_from_fix: new entry appended after the deletion loop; fix appends before dist.barrier so retention sees the new entry

relation_statement: Module outputs under CUDA-graph replay must equal the eager execution reference when activation recompute (checkpointing) is enabled for the same module.
observable_signal: output divergence between graph replay and an eager reference execution of the captured module
validity_precondition: activation recompute via tensor_parallel.checkpoint combined with CUDA graph capture of the same module (warmup or capture phase active)
evidence_from_issue: tensor_parallel.checkpoint runs CheckpointFunction during CUDA graph warmup, causing graph capture to record stale recomputed activations
evidence_from_fix: recomputing the saved forward inside the graph context corrupts the captured graph because random states and saved tensors get rewritten between warmup and capture; on replay the graph produces values that do not match the eager reference

relation_statement: Ratio statistics must be averaged only over mask-valid byte positions, not the full padded tensor, under guard that batches contain padded positions.
observable_signal: computed true_ratio/average_prob compared against a masked-mean recomputation; systematic downward bias when padding fraction is high
validity_precondition: ratio-loss computation on variable-length byte batches with padding present
evidence_from_issue: H-Net ratio loss averaged over padded positions — wrong target ratio under variable-length batches
evidence_from_fix: means were taken over the full padded byte tensor instead of byte_mask-valid positions; padded zeros shrank both quantities toward 0, biasing the ratio-loss target

relation_statement: Repeated optimizer state-increment calls carrying the same logical step (one per parameter subgroup) must leave the bias-correction factors identical, so all subgroups apply the same Adam step.
observable_signal: betta1_t/betta2_t values observed across subgroup calls within one logical step; divergence of updated weights between subgroups given identical inputs
validity_precondition: CPU-offloaded Adam with multiple subgroup optimizer calls per logical step (ZeRO-3 sub_group_size > 0)
evidence_from_issue: IncrementStep non-idempotent across same-step subgroup updates — bias-correction drifts between subgroups
evidence_from_fix: first call takes the multiplicative branch, second falls through to the pow-recompute branch computing a different floating-point value, so subgroups see different betta1_t

relation_statement: Input jitter must be applied to the router input before gating, not to the logits after gating, whenever input jitter is enabled in training.
observable_signal: none_runtime: the jitter insertion point is a code-order property; its downstream effect on z-loss gradient direction is statistical rather than a crisp runtime predicate
validity_precondition: MoE TopKRouter with moe_input_jitter_eps > 0 and training=True
evidence_from_issue: MoE input jitter applied AFTER gating instead of before, jittering gradients not inputs
evidence_from_fix: routing called apply_input_jitter(logits) AFTER computing logits; jittering logits changes Z-loss reference and z-loss gradient direction, silently degrading load balancing

relation_statement: Init-time collective broadcasts of parameters must stay outside the autograd graph so that backward never differentiates through a synchronization op.
observable_signal: parameters carrying a grad_fn / broadcast node in their autograd history after engine init; gradient mismatch vs a run with non-differentiable broadcast
validity_precondition: engine init broadcast of model parameters with requires_grad=True (ZeRO 1/2 broadcast path)
evidence_from_issue: init broadcast tracked through autograd — backward through synchronization op silently corrupts gradients
evidence_from_fix: c10d::broadcast_ has no registered autograd kernel; autograd traverses the broadcast op and computes incorrect gradients silently

relation_statement: The readout (output projection) weights must be initialized to zero, per the muP prescription, when use_mup is enabled.
observable_signal: Norm of ff_out weights immediately after reset_parameters: any nonzero value under muP witnesses the overwrite by init_normal.
validity_precondition: model.use_mup=true; reset_parameters invoked from __init__
evidence_from_issue: ff_out readout reset overwrites muP zero-init weights with normal-distribution values
evidence_from_fix: reset_parameters always called init_normal on ff_out, including under muP where ff_out must be initialized to zero; breaks the muP coordinate-check property; fix skips init_normal when use_mup

relation_statement: The total gradient norm across the PP group must be the L2 reduction (sqrt of summed squares) not a sum-of-norms under guard: pipeline parallelism.
observable_signal: Computed total_grad_norm magnitude vs the true global L2 norm; resulting clip factor.
validity_precondition: pipeline parallelism (mesh dim 'pp'), MoEFusedV2Optimizer in use
evidence_from_issue: reduces PP grad norm with _combine_norm (sum-of-norms) instead of _reduce_norm — over-counts gradient magnitude
evidence_from_fix: _combine_norm added rank-local norms instead of squaring/all-reducing/sqrt, over-estimating global norm
